correctness.rationale: The exact piecewise toral definition is reproduced; direct substitutions and B^2 A=[[1,9/2],[0,1]] prove the two full primitive-three intervals, and A^3 has saddle multipliers at the two isolated cycles. The standalone rational checker exactly tiles the closed torus square into 128 affine third-iterate cells with total area one, solves all modulo-one fixed equations with offsets in {-1,0,1}^2 including boundaries, and verifies all 32 raw point and 12 segment candidates belong to the proposed union. The reverse inclusion and arclength are independently derived algebraically in RESULT.md. This is a proof for all real points, not finite parameter sampling.

value.rationale: The originating paper singles out eta=1/3 as the nonhyperbolic boundary of the first mixing side. An exact classification there is a natural dynamical problem: two continuum families of neutral three-cycles coexist with two isolated hyperbolic saddle cycles. The geometric length 4/9*(1+sqrt(2)+sqrt(5)) is a nontrivial exact invariant and makes explicit the transition from hyperbolic behavior to nearby elliptic islands. Exhaustiveness and boundary treatment substantially exceed a routine orbit substitution.
